messages.subject: Frequency/Weight Statement?
parts:
Hello,

I have some polygon data that has uneven amounts of people in each polygon and I want to account for this when model building. With other packages (software), I have seen this done through a frequency or weight statement. Does something like that exist in this package?

For example, say I have crime data where each observation contains information for a city block. I want to model the amount of thefts, but I want to account for the fact that some city blocks might have 10 people while some might have 500.

Thanks for all your help! This is a great package.

Kelsey

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Frequency/Weight Statement?
parts:
On Mon, 2015-06-15 at 19:46 -0700, Kelsey Osterloo wrote:

> For example, say I have crime data where each observation contains
> information for a city block. I want to model the amount of thefts,
> but I want to account for the fact that some city blocks might have 10
> people while some might have 500.

Hi

this is done through the likelihood spesification, like for the Poisson
or neg.binomial case, you define this as an offset, like

y ~ offset(log(people)) + ...

or through the argument 'E', see inla.doc("poisson")

hope this helps ;-)

Best
H




--
Håvard Rue
